candidates.tagline: Built to end SpaceX's monopoly. Lasted 10 minutes.
candidates.story: On November 15, 2026, ULA's Vulcan Centaur rocket failed 10 minutes after liftoff on its 'return to flight' mission — only its 5th ever launch — destroying all 40 Amazon Project Kuiper satellites on board. It was ULA's first total mission failure in 20 years; Amazon, which had booked 38 Vulcan flights for its Starlink competitor, must now rely on SpaceX to launch its anti-SpaceX constellation.
candidates.why_funny: The rocket designed to end SpaceX's stranglehold on launches forced Amazon to book more SpaceX flights for its own Starlink competitor — the moment the rivalry was resolved, it was resolved by SpaceX winning by default.
candidates.alt: ULA Vulcan Centaur rocket on the launch pad at Cape Canaveral during the rollout for its first flight in January 2024, showing the full two-stage rocket and all six solid rocket boosters against a clear sky

candidates.tagline: BYD's flagship SUV shipped with the front and rear wheels literally on backwards.
candidates.story: On November 11, 2026, BYD apologized after its flagship Da Tang electric SUV was delivered to customers with front and rear wheel rims swapped — wider 9J rims fitted to the front axle and narrower 8J rims on the rear — because supplier Hubei Boyu Industrial entered a coding error. BYD's official statement: 'dedicated testing showed no safety impact.'
candidates.why_funny: The world's #1 EV maker delivered its marquee launch SUV with the wheels on backwards because someone typed a wrong code — and their reassurance that this is fine is somehow less reassuring than the error itself.
candidates.alt: BYD Da Tang electric SUV parked outside, the wheel size mismatch visible between front and rear axles — the result of a supplier coding error that swapped wider rear rims to the front and narrower front rims to the rear
